definitions.definition: The surroundings, circumstances, environment, background or settings that determine, specify, or clarify the meaning of an event or other occurrence.

quote.citation: 2012 September 7, Phil McNulty, “Moldova 0-5 England”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: The display and result must be placed in the context that was it was against a side that looked every bit their Fifa world ranking of 141 - but England completed the job with efficiency to record their biggest away win in 19 years.

definitions.definition: (linguistics) The text in which a word or passage appears and which helps ascertain its meaning.
(archaeology) The surroundings and environment in which an artifact is found and which may provide important clues about the artifact's function and/or cultural meaning.
(mycology) The trama or flesh of a mushroom.
(logic) For a formula: a finite set of variables, which set contains all the free variables in the given formula.
(programming) The data (register contents, program counter value, etc.) needed to switch to another thread of execution.
(obsolete) To knit or bind together; to unite closely.

quote.citation: 1638, Richard Younge, The Drunkard's Character: Or, a True Drunkard with Such Sinnes as Raigne in Him:
quote.text: The whole worlds frame, which is contexted onely by commerce and contracts.

quote.citation: 1623, Owen Feltham, Resolves: Divine, Moral, Political:
quote.text: If the Subiect bee Historie, or contexted Fable, then I hold it better put in Prose, or Blanks: for ordinarie discourse neuer shewes so well in Meeter

definitions.definition: (obsolete) Knit or woven together; close; firm.

quote.text: The skynne is composed & context and woven with thredes and vaynes.
